_comment: Code-search workspace pack — Serena (symbolic navigation) and Octocode (semantic/AST/graph retrieval) for ONE project. COMMON TO EVERY ROLE: the rows are root-level loader rows, so orchestrator, backend, research, reviewer, critic, docs, ux and standard sessions all receive the same static mcp__serena__*/mcp__octocode__* surface; no preset lists them and none can hide them. WORKSPACE-SCOPED, NOT MACHINE-WIDE: this is deliberately NOT profile/mcp-servers.json, because that list is projected into $DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml and a symbol server bound to one repository would then serve every project on the machine. scripts/dsh-mcp-sync.mjs --spec <this> --project <dir> --out <patch> renders the rows into an overlay the operator passes with --patch for that repository instance; nothing is written to the harness home. Owner: backend, task-mwbw9fmt-speqo9.

servers.description: Serena 2.1.0 (oraios/serena; the application is GPL-3.0-or-later, its SolidLSP library MIT): language-server symbolic navigation — find_symbol, find_referencing_symbols, get_symbols_overview, plus initial_instructions (the connection manual its own prompt demands). Read-only surface fixed by profile/serena-context.yml; no edit, memory, file-read or shell tools are loaded.

_notes.license: Serena the application is GPL-3.0-or-later (SolidLSP alone is MIT). This pack launches the user-installed binary as a separate process and ships no Serena code, so the kit is not a derivative work; a downstream redistribution of Serena itself would carry the GPL.
_notes.why-binary: Provisioned by `uv tool install serena-agent==2.1.0` into ~/.local/bin, so the row launches the installed, pinned console script. `uvx` would resolve the same pin on every launch and add seconds to every restart.
_notes.context: profile/serena-context.yml uses fixed_tools, which REPLACES Serena's default set. Measured on 2.1.0: without `--agent-interface tools` Serena 2.1 defaults to the REPL facade and exposes serena_repl instead of per-operation tools.
_notes.project: --project-from-cwd reads the project from the bridge's cwd (the row carries <project> as cwd); no machine path is baked into this file.
_notes.privacy: the web dashboard is off, and SERENA_USAGE_REPORTING=false stops the anonymous startup ping the server otherwise sends to oraios-software.de.
_notes.state: Serena stores its per-project cache and project.yml under <project>/.serena — tool state, not source (ignored by .gitignore).

servers.description: Octocode 0.29.2 (Apache-2.0, Muvon/octocode): conceptual/semantic retrieval, AST structural search and the Tree-sitter relationship graph. Wrapped by profile/octocode-readonly-guard.mjs, which hides and refuses the one write parameter (structural_search rewrite/update_all).

_notes.no-lsp: Octocode exposes LSP tools only when `mcp --with-lsp <command>` is passed. The row does not pass it, so the LSP surface does not exist (proved by tools/list).
_notes.read-only: structural_search can write files when `update_all` or `rewrite` is supplied. Prompt guidance is not an enforcement point, so the server row runs the kit's guard: it removes those two parameters from tools/list and answers a tools/call that carries them with a JSON-RPC error, before Octocode sees it. Measured: the guarded tools/list schema has no update_all/rewrite.
_notes.config: profile/octocode-config.toml disables the 1.1 GB FastEmbed reranker (the measured startup blocker) and keeps mcp_index=false, so the MCP server serves an existing index read-only; `octocode index` is the one setup step that builds it.
_notes.state: Octocode keeps its index outside source: ~/.local/share/octocode/<project-hash>/storage, measured 2026-11-11.
_notes.runner: node launches the guard, which spawns the provisioned `octocode mcp --path .` in the same cwd and proxies JSON-RPC without interpreting results.
